cards.title: Everything that happened, in order
cards.text: 30 on-track passes, 2 pit stops, every starter at the flag.

cards.title: 22 places changed hands on track before the first lap was done
cards.text: 22 cars into the first corner on cold tyres and full tanks.
bullets: Bearman and Colapinto gained the most by the end of it, 4 places each
cards.note: Most of this is the pack sorting itself out. Some of it decides the sprint.

cards.title: 3 incidents looked at
cards.text: Every one of them logged by race control during the sprint.
bullets: First up, lap 1: Hulkenberg, leaving the track and gaining an advantage
1 ended in a penalty and 2 left for after the sprint

cards.title: 8 passes on this lap alone
cards.text: Only moves made on track count here, at racing speed.
bullets: 8 different drivers gained a place on this lap
cards.note: Early on, with full tanks and the order still settling.

cards.title: Yellow flags out 1 time
cards.text: Race control waves a yellow for anything on or near the track that should not be there.
bullets: A yellow means slow down and do not overtake in that part of the track

cards.title: Albon starts P22. Where does he finish?
cards.text: 17 laps to make up ground from there.

cards.title: Lap 2: contact between Perez and Alonso at Turn 3. What do you give?
cards.text: Race control has flagged it and it lands on your desk. Same call the stewards had to make.

outcomes.none: You let it go. Nobody loses a place at a desk, and the driver behind spends the rest of the race on the radio.
outcomes.5: Five seconds gets added at the next stop, or to the final time if there is no stop left. Usually one position, sometimes none.
outcomes.10: Ten seconds is a real punishment and it almost always costs track position, which is why teams argue so hard about it.

cards.reveal: The stewards gave Perez a 10s penalty. He still finished P22.

cards.title: 8 passes on this lap alone
cards.text: Only moves made on track count here, at racing speed.
bullets: 7 different drivers gained a place on this lap
cards.note: Early on, with full tanks and the order still settling.

cards.title: Hadjar: 4 passes
cards.text: More than anybody else out there, in a Red Bull.
bullets: P8 on the grid, P9 at the flag
cards.note: Only moves made on track count, with the car ahead at racing speed.

cards.title: Track between 37°C and 41°C during the sprint
cards.text: Track temperature changes how much grip the tyres find and how fast they wear. No rain was recorded during the sprint.

cards.title: Bortoleto: 6 laps within a second of the car ahead
cards.text: The longest unbroken run like it in the sprint, from lap 2 to lap 7, at racing speed.
bullets: 2 other drivers had a run of five laps or more like it
cards.note: Following closely costs the car downforce and cooks the front tyres, so sitting there is harder than it looks.

cards.title: 9 lap times deleted
cards.text: The white line is the track, and the lap simply stops counting if you leave it.
bullets: Stroll lost 3 that way, more than anybody
cards.note: Keep doing it and it turns into a penalty.

cards.title: Hadjar hit 340 km/h
cards.text: The fastest car in a straight line is often not the fastest car over a lap.
bullets: Hadjar did it in a Red Bull
cards.note: Top speed says as much about wing level, and about sitting in somebody's tow, as it does about the engine.

cards.title: Antonelli takes the lead from Hamilton
cards.text: A pass for the lead, made on track at racing speed.

cards.title: 1 penalty handed out
cards.text: Given by the stewards during the sprint.
bullets: Perez: a 10s penalty for causing a collision
cards.note: A time penalty is served at the next stop, or added to the final time when there is no stop left.

cards.title: Who has the fastest lap on the board at the flag?
cards.text: It usually lands late, when the car is light and the track has rubber all over it.
cards.reveal: Antonelli on lap 17, 1:31.607, in a Mercedes.

cards.title: Antonelli had the quickest median racing lap
cards.text: No lap 1, no laps in or out of the pits, nothing behind the safety car or the VSC, and the slow outliers trimmed. It does not always match the result.

cards.title: Perez went the other way: 4 places lost
cards.text: Qualifying promised one thing and the sprint delivered another.
bullets: P18 on the grid, P22 at the flag
1 stop when most of the field made none
Qualifying rewards whoever can put one lap together. A sprint asks for 17 of them

cards.title: Albon: P22 on the grid, P18 at the flag
cards.text: 4 places gained.
bullets: 3 on-track passes along the way

cards.title: 20 of 22 cars never stopped
cards.text: One set of tyres took most of the field to the flag.
bullets: On one set the whole way: Mediums for 18, softs for Alonso and Bottas
cards.note: Every lap you stretch is a lap you do not lose in the pit lane.

cards.title: Antonelli: 1:31.607
cards.text: The quickest anybody went all sprint, in a Mercedes.
bullets: Set on lap 17 of 17, late on, where they usually land
By then the fuel is nearly gone and the car is at its lightest
A sprint has never paid a point for it

cards.title: Antonelli wins it
cards.text: P1 Antonelli · P2 Hamilton · P3 Norris.
bullets: After 17 laps, Hamilton crossed the line 2.745s behind

cards.title: How far behind was Hamilton at the flag?
cards.text: 17 laps, about 26 minutes of racing, and it comes down to this one number.
